condition: acute symptomatic severe hypertension 224 over 128 with giddiness in young adult on therapy
level_rationale: A home blood pressure reading of 224 over 128 right now accompanied by 1 hour of acute dizziness in a 29-year-old adult on daily blood pressure tablets represents symptomatic severe hypertension requiring immediate hospital evaluation and monitored blood pressure management, whereas a home reading of 148 over 92 with 1 hour of mild dizziness in the same treated hypertensive patient reflects suboptimal outpatient blood pressure control appropriate for an outpatient clinic medication review rather than emergency care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Indian English core dialect lexicon swap ('dizziness' vs 'giddiness', retained in everyday_paraphrase) + single measured blood-pressure de-escalation control (-cf, 224 over 128 to 148 over 92, L4 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 29, daily blood pressure tablets, 1 hour of mild dizziness this morning, and home cuff reading 224 over 128 right now) with zero stranded emergency red flags in f1-f3 and zero stated negatives. Changing only measured cuff values in fact f4 ('reads 224 over 128' to 'reads 148 over 92') follows Rule A's first-choice measured-value design and Rule D uniqueness, shifting care cleanly from emergency hospital care (level 4) to outpatient clinic antihypertensive review (level 2).
